subject: BlueCrest renewal — concession escalation / exec review
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie@bluecrest.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueCrest Procurement <procurement@bluecrest.io>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@bluecrest.io>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal: need to discuss concessions to proceed

Marcus —

Thanks for the heads up on the Feb 15 renewal. We ran this through finance this morning and unfortunately our budget has tightened significantly for Q1. To get this over the finish line we need material concessions: a 25% list-level discount, a 12-month term reset to align billing cadence, and an SLA credit (99.99% uptime commitment or an equivalent service credit).

If Redwood can’t provide flexibility on at least a subset of those items, we’ll likely have to move to an alternative solution. We’re asking you to escalate — procurement and I need a response that we can present to our CFO today.

Attached: current POC and procurement checklist (see procurement@bluecrest.io).

— Sophie
Sophie Park
Head of Data Platforms
BlueCrest Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@bluecrest.io>
Date: 2027-01-10T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: need to discuss concessions to proceed

Sophie — thank you for the transparency and flagging timing. I hear you on budget pressure and the three asks. I’m escalating internally now to arm-wrestle options and will get you a firm response within 48 hours.

Quick ask for your team — can you confirm the primary decision deadline (is it EOD tomorrow?) and whether the 12-month reset is a hard requirement vs. a preference? Also happy to hop on a quick 20–30m call with Tom or procurement if that helps.

I’ll follow up by EOD on Tuesday with what we can offer.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Date: 2027-01-10T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal — escalate for exec concession (RDW-4352)

Team — forwarding Sophie’s note. BlueCrest is leaning toward an alternative unless we provide material concessions. Key asks from customer: 25% discount, 12-month term reset, and SLA credit. Procurement/Finance need an answer urgently (likely by EOD tomorrow).

Context: BlueCrest is a mid-market account with ~$1.2M ARR run-rate on our platform and has been a stable customer for 18 months. Renewal due 2027-02-15. They’re strategic in our analytics vertical in the northeast and there’s some channel overlap with partners we’re cultivating.

Request: Ben—can you run a concession options matrix (impact to ARR, margin, precedent) and propose 2 packages: one {minimal revenue-protecting} option and one {customer-saving} option that we can present to the execs for sign-off. Vivek—please include quick financial impact and whether a term reset is feasible from billing ops. Priyom — tagging for visibility; I’ll need final approval to offer anything beyond standard pricing.

I’ve attached the current M&A and the original proposal.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal — escalate for exec concession (RDW-4352)

Team — ran through scenarios (attached: concession_calc_bluecrest_20270111.xlsx). Summary:

Option A (protective): 12% one-year discount; 6-month SLA credit capped at $40k; no term reset. Net impact ~ -$145k NPV over 12 months.

Option B (customer-save): 20% one-year discount; 12-month term reset as requested; SLA credit $75k (or 1 month free equivalent). Net impact ~ -$265k NPV over 12 months and sets a pricing precedent in our NE analytics cohort.

Notes: a full 25% discount + 12-month reset would push impact north of -$330k and is hard to justify for a ~$1.2M ARR account. If we go the Option B route we should require a one-time commitment (add a 12-month auto-renew clause) and mark this as a limited, non-precedent concession.

Attachments: concession_calc_bluecrest_20270111.xlsx, proposal_v2_redlined.pdf

Ben Carter
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T11:56:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal — escalate for exec concession (RDW-4352)

Quick ops take: term reset is doable but will require a billing amendment and one-time invoice adjustment; timeline to enact = 5–7 business days after signed SOW. If we include a 12-month reset we must also clear it with Finance for revenue recognition (minor deferral).

Recommendation (ops + margin): Offer Option A as primary: 12% discount + $40k SLA credit + maintain same term dates (no reset). As a stretch that I’d push to exec: 15% discount + $40k SLA credit + one-time billing adjustment (not a full 12-month reset) to help their cash flow. Option B (20% + 12-month reset) is high risk for precedent and revenue.

I’m happy to join a quick call with customer ops to explain the billing mechanics.

— Vivek
Director, Sales Operations
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: BlueCrest renewal — escalate for exec concession (RDW-4352)

Thanks for the rapid analysis. After reviewing Ben’s impact numbers and Vivek’s ops constraints, here’s what I authorize to get the deal preserved while controlling precedent:

Approved package (authorized):
- 12% one-year list-level discount (applies to next 12 months)
- $40,000 SLA credit applied as a one-time invoice credit (applies after renewal)
- One-time billing adjustment to assist cash flow (equivalent to moving one month’s payment to the next billing cycle), but we will not do a full 12-month term reset.

Conditions:
1) Customer signs amended SOW and DocuSign within 5 business days of our offer.
2) Add explicit non-precedent language and a 12-month auto-renew clause.
3) Finance to confirm revenue recognition path before amendment is executed.

Marcus — please communicate this package to Sophie and procurement, include the amended proposal (I want to review the DocuSign packet before it goes out).

Priyom Das
VP, Sales — East
priyom_das@redwood.com

- 12% one-year discount on the renewed term (applies to next 12 months)
- $40,000 one-time SLA credit applied as invoice credit after renewal

- Agreement will include non-precedent language and a 12-month auto-renew clause.
